newsitem.title: USA: Airlines sue San Francisco on domestic partners law.
newsitem.headline: Airlines sue San Francisco on domestic partners law.

text.p: The nation's largest airline trade group on Tuesday sued the city of San Francisco, challenging a city law that forces companies to offer the same benefits to domestic partners as married couples.

The Air Transport Association's lawsuit, filed in U.S. District Court in San Francisco, contends the city's regulations would intrude on federal law, impede interstate commerce and violate the U.S. Constitution.
The city's attorneys said they would defend the law.

Last year, San Francisco's governing board of supervisors passed the local ordinance, which requires companies doing business with the city to provide equal benefits to spouses and employees' unmarried partners -- gay or heterosexual.
Because San Francisco International Airport is owned by the city, every airline must comply with the law in order to continue operating at the airport, the association said.
"For the airlines, this is not a moral issue and has nothing to do with sexual orientation," association President Carol Hallett said in a statement.
Under federal law, local governments are not allowed to mandate what benefits airlines offer, or do not offer, to their employees, Hallett said.

Airlines have always been governed by federal rather than local laws "because it would be impossible to operate in hundreds of communities with different and possibly contradictory local ordinances," Hallett said.
The association is seeking a court order that would shield the airlines from the city's domestic partners rule, which is scheduled to take effect on June 1.
San Francisco City Attorney Louise Renne said she would review the lawsuit but added, "it's the policy of the city of San Francisco and we're going to defend it."

In recent months, several prominent San Francisco companies said they would comply with the city's rule. Chevron Corp. and BankAmerica Corp. both said they would extend domestic partners' benefits to U.S. employees.
The Air Transport Association's lawsuit was filed against the city of San Francisco, the San Francisco Human Rights Commission and the San Francisco Airports Commission.
The Airline Industrial Relations Conference -- representing labor attorneys for the major airlines -- joined in the lawsuit.

The Air Transport Association is the oldest and largest airline trade group in the United States. It has 22 U.S. and three international airline members, which together transports more than 95 percent of all passenger and cargo traffic in the United States.
